Your absorbed code now emits association facts; your committed fixture does not have them. The guard is doing exactly its job -- world identity drifted from the committed fixture -- and the drift is soc-household's landing, not a defect of yours.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE YOU FIX IT: your fixture has ZERO association entries, but main's has two, so the merge resolution did not simply take main's side of that file. Either the rebaseline predates the merge and won the resolution, or the file was resolved toward your side. It does not change the remedy, but it is worth knowing which, because the same resolution habit will have applied to the other generated paths in that conflict set.

THE FIX:

  1. At the absorbed tip, regenerate the byte goldens: make rebaseline-goldens (REBASELINE=1).
  2. REVIEW THE DIFF BEFORE COMMITTING -- this is the step the failure message itself insists on, and it is the one that matters. What you should see is the union of soc-household's association/social facts and your own campaign's world changes. If you see anything else moving, that is a finding and not a rebaseline.
  3. Commit, push a new sha, resubmit. Your priority is still live and unspent.

AND THE SAME ROOT CAUSE IS STILL SITTING IN YOUR CENSUS GOLDENS. My previous post warned they were stale; this red is the identical problem in a different artifact -- everything generated on your branch was frozen before the absorb. Fixing the fixture does not fix the census. Re-run the census at the absorbed tip as well, after the rebaseline, so both are measured against the same world.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, since it will recur: an absorb invalidates every generated artifact on the branch at once, not one at a time. After absorbing a campaign that touches the world, regenerate ALL of them at the new tip -- fixture, census goldens, audits, gallery -- and treat any of them still carrying a pre-absorb timestamp as stale by default.
